A1.justification: Both PDFs describe RAPID and provide readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices. Relocated sections and renumbered case studies can be matched, with no material reading gaps.

before.justification: v2 reports original benchmark experiments, component ablations, caption evaluations, training dynamics, and human assessments, including Tables 1-3 and Appendix E.

after.justification: v3 retains those original results and adds experiments on other MLLMs, caption-check auditing, training variants, and computational costs.

M1.justification: The default RAPID pipeline remains unchanged. Appendices E.3-E.7 add experimental procedural variants: stricter hasSol checking, length-penalized VPO, GRPO fine-tuning of the external reasoner, and using the same MLLM for perception and reasoning. These are limited adaptations rather than replacements of the main method.

E1.justification: Both versions use ViRL39K for training, the same seven reasoning benchmarks, and the same general vision-language evaluation suite. The new backbone experiments and diagnostic controls do not establish additional dataset, domain, or task coverage.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds GRPO-trained Qwen2.5-VL-7B with best-of-8 selection using VisualPRM-8B-v1.1, SRPO-7B, ReVPT-7B, and DeepEyes-7B, substantially extending comparison to verification, reflection, and tool-based approaches. Appendix F.3 also adds OmniCaptioner-7B and MM-Eureka-7B to the caption-quality comparison, which previously compared models with and without VPO.

E3.justification: New evaluation designs include a 400-generation manual validity audit, an additional 100-step GRPO recovery experiment for the 7B model, controlled caption lengths, InternVL3 configurations, and external-reasoner training with GRPO group size four. Existing benchmark splits and main accuracy definitions are retained; these are added protocols rather than evidence that the original experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Appendices E.3-E.7 substantially expand tests of the caption checker and its failures, reasoning recovery after VPO, caption length as an alternative explanation, reasoner fine-tuning, and same-model reasoning. v3 also adds cross-family component ablations and caption-quality comparisons. The earlier human evaluation and extensive case studies are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Human agreement reporting is unchanged. The new checker confusion counts and error rates are performance point estimates, not a new uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: Existing main RAPID scores are retained, including 53.2% for Qwen2.5-VL-7B with Qwen3-8B. New results include InternVL3-8B reaching 51.9% with RAPID versus its 44.6% baseline, and reasoner fine-tuning yielding 53.3% versus 53.2%. Numerous diagnostic and comparator results are added. Table 12 reports identical 51.1% accuracies for both Qwen3 length conditions, so its claimed small improvement is not supported by the displayed values.

T1.justification: The VPO and GRPO formulations in Equations 1-4 remain unchanged. Appendix E.5 newly defines the length-control reward r_len(y, n_target) = -alpha|n_target - n_y| for an experimental variant. No new theorem or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution list, and conclusion retain the same central claims: perception-reasoning decoupling, reasoning-aligned caption optimization through VPO, and inference-time scaling by replacing the external reasoner without retraining.

C2.justification: v3 adds substantive interpretations concerning caption/solution coexistence, model-size-dependent reasoning recovery, the inadequacy of caption length alone, and diminishing returns from adapting a strong reasoner. Appendix E.5 strengthens the earlier speculative discussion into a causal claim that length has been eliminated as a confounder. Appendix G adds proposed roles alongside unified models. The original limitations text is relocated unchanged.

D1.justification: Table 5 adds H20 GPU counts, wall-clock times, GPU-hours, and rental-cost estimates beyond v2's computational proxies. New experiments disclose the length target of 650, penalty weight 0.0003, and reasoner GRPO group size four. A reproducibility statement promises scripts at the existing project link; actual availability cannot be established from the PDFs.

R1.justification: The related-work distinctions in Section 2 are retained. v3 adds citations supporting reflection/tool comparisons and length control, while Appendix G extends positioning toward RAPID as a complementary data engine for unified models and a framework related to expert-based systems.

P1.justification: Existing prose receives limited editing, including replacing 'holistic' with 'standard' captions and updating the conference header. Limitations move from Appendix H to A, and new experimental, discussion, ethics, reproducibility, and acknowledgment sections are inserted. Most existing narrative and section ordering remain recognizable.

P2.justification: v3 substantially extends the empirical displays with new backbone, cost, and diagnostic tables, an expanded Table 1, a two-panel caption-comparison Figure 21, and InternVL3 panels in the training plots. Figure 10 corrects its baseline legends from 'w/o GRPO' to 'w/ GRPO'. Existing case-study images and most original plots are retained.

improvement.justification: Compared with v2's VPO validation confined to Qwen2.5-VL, v3 adds InternVL3 evidence, direct failure analyses, additional controls, and concrete hardware timings, improving validation and practical transparency. These gains are moderated by weaknesses in the new analyses: Table 12 displays identical accuracies despite claiming improvement, and Appendix E.3 gives an unqualified reliability interpretation despite a 26.32% false-positive rate among invalid captions. The net quality gain is positive but limited.
